gen-gf-unica-one-gf-nata-sans: Commanding up top, Unica One keeps every stroke at a single thickness. Nata Sans below it is a plain sans with a large central band and open curves, and that quiet technical-pen steadiness is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-nobile: Nobile reads smooth and contemporary, with capitals barely taller than lowercase and mouths left open. Nobile as a sans-serif carries a long stretch of text without tiring, while Unica One's neon-tube thickness keeps the headline loud.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-nokora: Unica One has no tilt to its round letters, every curve cut with the same bare, upright stroke. And Nokora lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase with a wide s, so a long passage feels dense and welcoming.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic is a modern sans-serif with a welcoming gap in its c and capitals sitting barely above lowercase. Next to Unica One's fixed-pressure stylus line, it feels softer and lighter.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans fills most of its letter height with lowercase body and a wide c, so it reads easily in sans-serif text. And Unica One, cut from one gauge of tubing, gives the heading a lean, distinctive edge.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Unica One is all tubing-straight lines, arches as thick as stems. Its heavy-handed focus suits headings, while Noto Sans Adlam, a sans-serif with tall, full c, s and z and well-spaced curve endings, handles the text.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjo: Unica One holds a calm, unvarying weight from word to word, with daylight inside every curve. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined adds generous space between curve ends and stems, so sans text sits quietly under the heading.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-: Unica One draws every letter with a flat, unvarying line, which gives it a strong, distinctive look. But Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs, a sans with outward-pointing tips and a high x-height, is what makes the pair feel modern.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Loud, lean and unmistakable: Unica One draws its steady line with no pressure variation at all. It commands the heading, while Noto Sans Armenian, a sans-serif with full round letters, does the quiet reading.
